pages.text:
Emergency Preparedness andResponse in Madagascar
In emergencies, WFP provides unconditionalfood and cash assistance to affected people,combined with anticipatory actions, capacity-building, rapid response and nutritionalsupplementation for pregnant andbreastfeeding women and girls, as well aschildren.
Country context
Madagascar ranks among the countries mostexposed to extreme weather events.
Droughts, cyclones, and economic challengescontinue to fuel food insecurity, especially in thevulnerable regions of the Great South andSouth-East.
Since 2024, irregular rainfall during theagricultural planting season, coupled with theimpact of five tropical storms and cyclonesduring the first semester of 2025, furtherstrained an already fragile humanitariancontext.
The El Niño phenomenon has intensified thesechallenges, severely affecting crop yields andleading to worsening food insecurity.
Additionally, flooding during the harvest periodin the Greater South-East caused substantial croplosses, amplifying the effects of the early leanseason. Climate change is expected to increaseboth the frequency and severity of these eventsover time.
2024 Key Figures
1,306,250 people received unconditional assistance
USD 3.7 million ofcash assistance and16,226 MT of foodwere distributed tobeneficiaries
According to the latest IPC analysis, 1.2 million people are facing highlevels of acute food insecurity (IPC Phase 3 or above) between May andSeptember 2025. For the first time since Cyclone Freddy in 2023, emergencylevels of food insecurity (IPC Phase 4) have been recorded among 29,000people. Conditions are expected to deteriorate during the peak of the leanseason (February-April 2026), with 110,000 people expected to face IPCPhase 4.
In Madagascar, WFP implements an integrated approach to disasterpreparedness and response. This includes:
Emergency Preparedness: Building capacities of government andhumanitarian partners, pre-positioning food and logistics supplies andupdating contingency plans in close coordination with nationalinstitutions (BNGRC, CPGU, DGM).Anticipatory Actions: Early-warning messages are disseminated, andpre-arranged funding for anticipatory cash transfers near high-risk areascan be rapidly released when trigger thresholds for droughts or cyclonesare reached.Rapid Response: Delivering hot meals or high-energy biscuits within 72hours of a disaster.Emergency Food Assistance: Unconditional food and cash assistanceare distributed to people affected by droughts or cyclones, typicallybetween October and April.Prevention of Malnutrition (PREVMA) and NutritionalSupplementation (MAM): Additional food rations or specializednutritious foods are distributed to children and pregnant andbreastfeeding women and girls, in collaboration with the RegionalNutrition Office (ORN).

WFP Emergency Response
Unconditional food and cash assistance for peopleaffected by drought and cyclones
During the lean season, between October and March, WFP providesunconditional food assistance to populations experiencing acute foodinsecurity, particularly in the Great South and Southeast where prolongeddroughts in recent years have significantly worsened living conditions.
Support is also extended to households in areas affected by cyclones andtropical storms, usually in the coastal regions of the Great South-East, includingVatovavy, Fitovinany, and Atsimo Atsinanana, and occasionally in the North, aswas the case for cyclone Gamane in 2024.
The standard food basket includes:
Rice or sorghumPulsesVegetable oil
For cash-based assistance, WFP provides 140,000 Ariary (approx. USD 27) perhousehold per month.
Prevention of Malnutrition (PREVMA) and Supplementation for ModerateAcute Malnutrition (MAM):
WFP combines unconditional food assistance with preventive nutrition andsupplementation efforts, aligned with WHO guidelines for the treatment ofwasting. The programme targets pregnant and breastfeeding women and girls(PBWG), as well as children aged 6–23 months and 6–59 months suffering frommoderate acute malnutrition (MAM), due to their heightened vulnerability.
During the lean season, PREVMA support is delivered through additional rationsand specialized nutritious foods to women and children aged 6-23 months whoare already receiving unconditional food assistance.
Throughout the year, nutrition supplementation for Moderate AcuteMalnutrition (MAM) is delivered in cycles of specialized nutritious foods forchildren aged 6-59 months. Anthropometric screenings are conducted duringunconditional distributions to identify children with signs of malnutrition. Severecases are referred to community health facilities for appropriate treatment andcare.
Nutrition assistance is coupled with social and behavior changecommunication (SBCC) activities and infant and young child feeding (IYCF)counselling, targeting both men and women to foster inclusive engagement inchild nutrition.
In 2024
43,116 Pregnant and Breastfeeding Women and Girls (PBWG) and 58,907 children aged 6-23 months were assisted with PREVMA assistance
184,986 children aged 6-59 months reached with MAM supplementation
Anticipatory Actions
Anticipatory actions are defined as the anticipation of foreseeable risks to actdays, weeks and sometimes even months before a climate shock occurs,mitigating the impact on food security, lives and livelihoods, and reducing acutehumanitarian impacts before they develop.
Anticipatory actions are delivered in the form of early warning messages, pre-positioned food, and cash that are ready to be distributed once a certainthreshold is reached. Given the predictable and recurrent nature of certainweather hazards in Madagascar, WFP is taking a proactive approach to protectlives and livelihoods more effectively, while reducing the long-term costs ofemergency response.
In 2024 - 2025
20,003 households received cash transfers and early warning messages USD 1.5 million have been disbursed Drought coverage in 11 communes across 2 districts and cyclone coveragenationwide

United Nations Humanitarian Air Service (UNHAS)
UNHAS has solidified its position as a key partner in deliveringhumanitarian assistance to Madagascar's most remote regions, byproviding safe and reliable air transport services to 52 organizationsacross 22 destinations. Its user base includes UN agencies (55%), NGOs(40%), diplomatic and donor missions (3%), and Red Cross/Red Crescentsocieties (2%).
In 2025, UNHAS launched an innovative pilot initiative in humanitarianlogistics, utilizing Unmanned Aerial Systems (UAS) — commonly knownas drones — to deliver small cargo such as high-energy biscuits, vaccines,medical supplies and shelter kits to hard-to-reach areas.
In 2024
3,563 passengers transported25,988 kg of humanitarian cargo transported58 special flights and 6 medical evacuations conducted
Supply Chain, the backbone of WFP’s emergencyresponse in Madagascar
The Supply Chain unit is instrumental in enabling WFP to deliverhumanitarian assistance across Madagascar, where efficient managementof goods and services is crucial to meet the needs of vulnerablecommunities.
Supply chain operations encompass the planning, procurement,transportation, storage, and distribution of food and humanitarian itemsto some of the country’s most inaccessible and remote areas.
In 2024
The Supply Chain unit handled a total volume of over 60,000 metrictons, successfully delivering nearly 29,000 MT of food commodities —including rice, pulses, fortified oil, and specialized nutritious products.
Thank you to our partners and donors for their continued support
Contact
Tania Goossens, Representative and Country Director - WFP Madagascar, tania.goossens@wfp.orgChiara Guccione, Head Partnerships and Reporting - WFP Madagascar, chiara.guccione@wfp.org Outman Badaoui, Head of Programme - WFP Madagascar, outman.badaoui@wfp.org
